compiled_state.title: [reconciler/applier]: inbound create for a bound issue whose snapshot lacks the dso-id label -> no applier-level dedup safety net (differ stand-down is the only guard)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview
Follow-up from the a666/b38a/38fd/4cc1 dedup-cluster resolution (PR #686). 

Bug 4354 (differ.py compute_mutations) prevents an inbound CREATE for an already-bound Jira issue by recognising the dso-id:<local_id> label IN THE SNAPSHOT and standing down. This is the production dedup and it is correct for the common case.

## Residual gap
There is a narrow transient window where the fetcher snapshot does NOT carry the dso-id label yet (e.g. fetched between an outbound bind and the label write-back propagating) but the binding DOES exist in bindings.json. In that window the snapshot differ cannot see the label, emits an inbound CREATE, and applier._apply_inbound_create has NO dedup guard of its own -> it would materialise a duplicate local ticket.

## Proposed (defense-in-depth, not urgent)
Add an optional inbound dedup guard in _apply_inbound_create keyed on binding_store.get_local_id(mutation.target) (the reverse index already exists, binding_store.py:229). On hit: write mapping + skip materialisation. Thread binding_store through BOTH _apply_typed call sites (applier.py ~2571 single-mutation + ~2740 loop). Omit story_branch SHA fields concern — this is production code. Note: an opus review judged this window narrow and the guard largely redundant with the 4354 differ suppression, hence priority 4.

## Scope note
This is the optional follow-up the user requested when choosing the honest-test-rewrite resolution for the dedup cluster. NOT a confirmed production defect.
